clue.text: Damaged, like Cotswolds manor house in quartet?

definitions.text: like Cotswolds manor house in quartet?
definitions.meaning: ... Norton, the Gloucestershire manor that names the first of T. S. Eliot's Four Quartets

explanation.walkthrough: The Cotswolds are hills in Gloucestershire, England; Eliot's poem 'Burnt Norton' takes its title from a manor house there.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scorched by fire is harmed, and Eliot's manor carries the same word in its name.

clue.text: A bare bath might have been provided here

definitions.text: A bare bath might have been provided here

indicators.note: the letters could have been put together in another order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somewhere a plain tub was laid on for bathers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bethabara is the place beyond the Jordan where John baptised (John 1:28), so a bath of a bare kind was indeed offered there; the letters of A BARE BATH rearrange to give it.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism by immersion is a ritual bath, and this biblical site is where John performed it.

clue.text: Asimov character seen to steal book

parts.note: to rob is to steal
OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A figure from Isaac Asimov's fiction is caught pinching a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov's stories are famous for their mechanical men, such as those in I, Robot.

clue.text: Indiscriminately hawk lots of chat on this

indicators.note: without any order or selection, so the letters are thrown together afresh

explanation.surface: A street trader peddles goods carelessly while gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indiscriminately' rearranges HAWK LOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast programme built around conversation is a place for chat.

clue.text: Possibly visit clue for old law book

indicators.note: the letters could possibly form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion to go and inspect a lead for an ancient legal text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges VISIT CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The third book of the Bible sets out priestly and ritual laws of ancient Israel.

clue.text: (see 16 Ac)

annotationWithheld.why: Clue is only '(see 16 Ac)'; the single clue 'Tragedy of one not taken on board — an amusing writer' serves two lights (KING/RING and LEAR), and the grid's RING does not fit the tragedy reading

clue.text: He was in love in Amsterdam, his creator feeling right inside

definitions.text: He was in love in Amsterdam, his creator feeling right inside

parts.words: He was in love in Amsterdam, his creator feeling right inside
parts.note: Love in Amsterdam is the first novel about Nicolas Freeling's Dutch detective; the author's name is the word feeling with R for right put in

explanation.surface: A man fell in love in Amsterdam while his maker felt emotion surge within.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds the author, not the hero: FEELING with R (right) inside gives FREELING, the Dutch-based novelist whose policeman first appeared in Love in Amsterdam (1962).
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Freeling's Amsterdam police inspector is the hero of Love in Amsterdam and later novels.

clue.text: Fully supported situation of Brontéan painter

definitions.text: Fully supported situation of Brontéan painter

parts.words: Fully supported situation of Brontéan painter
parts.note: Anne Brontë's heroine Helen Graham, an artist, rents Wildfell Hall, the novel being named for her status there

explanation.surface: An artist in a Brontë novel lives in a well-propped position.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Brontë's novel is The Tenant of Wildfell Hall; its heroine supports herself by painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Helen Graham occupies Wildfell Hall as a renter, the role named in the book's title.

clue.text: Mendicant from Cumberland

parts.note: a begging friar of the order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, linked by name to Cartmel in old Cumberland

explanation.surface: A beggar who has come down from the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumberland is a former county in north-west England, home of Cartmel Priory.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Friars are one of the mendicant orders, living by alms.

clue.text: American author seen in Germany, full of beer

definitions.meaning: Gertrude ..., the American writer who lived in Paris

definitions.text: seen in Germany, full of beer
definitions.meaning: a German beer mug, as seen filled in Bavarian beer halls

explanation.walkthrough: One word names both Gertrude the writer and the large German drinking mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Stein was an American modernist writer, and the same word is a German earthenware tankard.

clue.text: Moneylender's friend and murderer suggest early artificer

parts.note: Tubal is Shylock's friend in The Merchant of Venice
Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: Two figures from a moneylender's circle hint at an ancient craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis 4:22 names Tubal-cain as the first forger of bronze and iron tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis calls this descendant of Cain an instructor of every craftsman in metal.

clue.text: "Oh damn their Celtic twilight," Peter thought. "Thank God I'm —" (Eric Linklater, White Maa's Saga)

definitions.text: "Oh damn their Celtic twilight," Peter thought. "Thank God I'm —" (Eric Linklater, White Maa's Saga)

parts.words: "Oh damn their Celtic twilight," Peter thought. "Thank God I'm —" (Eric Linklater, White Maa's Saga)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: Peter rejects Celtic romance and claims Scandinavian descent instead

explanation.surface: A character in Linklater's novel scorns Celtic mist and thanks God for his own heritage.
explanation.walkthrough: Linklater was an Orkney writer; Orkney's heritage is Scandinavian rather than Celtic.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter sets his Scandinavian Viking ancestry against the Celtic twilight he dislikes.

clue.text: Joyce's youthful sitter

parts.note: the subject of a portrait painted when young, from Joyce's title A Portrait of the ... as a Young Man

explanation.surface: James Joyce has a young person posing for him.
explanation.walkthrough: A sitter is the subject of a portrait, and Joyce's novel is A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Dedalus is portrayed as a young creative figure in Joyce's novel.

clue.text: Friday writer

parts.note: the author of the 1982 science fiction novel Friday

explanation.surface: Someone who writes at the end of the working week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friday' looks like a day; it is the title of Robert A. Heinlein's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert A. Heinlein, the American science fiction author, published Friday in 1982.

clue.text: Innocent victims, exterminated in crusade

parts.note: Pope Innocent III launched the crusade that destroyed the Cathar heretics of southern France

explanation.surface: Blameless people were wiped out in a holy war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent' looks like 'blameless'; it is Pope Innocent III, whose crusade they suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cathars of Albi were the target of Innocent III's thirteenth-century crusade.

clue.text: Play strongly in favour of low score?

parts.note: to be all for something is to support it strongly
love is nil in tennis, the lowest score

explanation.surface: A sport keenly supported despite a feeble scoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: All for Love is John Dryden's tragedy of Antony and Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden's 1677 drama retells the story of Antony and Cleopatra for the stage.

clue.text: Poet showing the French caging a bird

indicators.note: the French article closes round the other pieces as a cage holds a bird

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
a martin is a bird of the swallow family

explanation.surface: A verse writer shows the French keeping a bird captive.
explanation.walkthrough: Alphonse de Lamartine was a French Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphonse de Lamartine wrote the Méditations poétiques, a landmark of French Romantic verse.

clue.text: Tragedy of one not taken on board — an amusing writer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Tragedy of one not taken on board — an amusing writer' covers two lights (this and 4-down LEAR); the grid's RING does not fit 'Tragedy of one not taken on board' (KING, as in KING LEAR), and no source gives the reading
annotationWithheld.clue: Tragedy of one not taken on board — an amusing writer

clue.text: Chap flowers in Simms book

parts.note: a guy is a chap
rivers are things that flow, flowers

explanation.surface: A man with blooms appears in a novel by Simms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' reads as blooms but means things that flow. Guy Rivers (1834) is a novel by William Gilmore Simms.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gilmore Simms, the American novelist, wrote Guy Rivers: A Tale of Georgia.

clue.text: Venetian nobleman in substitute for ode rigorously revised

indicators.note: the picked letters are reworked into a new order
the letters needed sit within the phrase ode rigorously

explanation.surface: A gentleman of Venice stands in for a poem that was strictly reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks ODE RIGOR out of 'ode rigorously', and 'revised' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderigo is the Venetian gentleman duped by Iago in Othello.

clue.text: Spenserian chatelaine associated with mother in old school

definitions.meaning: the lady who rules the House of Temperance in Spenser's Faerie Queene, Book II

definitions.text: associated with mother in old school
definitions.meaning: the word goes with mater ('mother') to make the phrase for one's old school or college

explanation.walkthrough: A chatelaine is the mistress of a great house; alma mater, 'nourishing mother', means one's former school.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser's mistress of the castle shares her name with the Latin word paired with 'mater' for a former school.

clue.text: Pile big boy upset reveals some fine bookbinding

indicators.note: knocked over and disturbed, so the letters fall in a new order

explanation.surface: A child knocks over a stack of volumes and uncovers some elegant binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges PILE BIG BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare word comes from Greek biblion 'book' and pegnunai 'to fasten', the craft of binding.

clue.text: Late support at church for Ambrose

parts.note: a bier supports the late, the dead
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Belated help at a church for a man named Ambrose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not tardy. Ambrose Bierce was the American writer of The Devil's Dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrose Bierce was the American satirist who wrote The Devil's Dictionary.

clue.text: Long distance writer

parts.note: the author of the 1974 novel Long Distance

explanation.surface: Someone who writes from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long distance' is the title of a novel by Penelope Mortimer.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope Mortimer, the English novelist, published Long Distance in 1974.

clue.text: "It happens to country like you, as soon as you dance with a fellow" (Edna O Brien, The Lonely Girl)

definitions.text: "It happens to country like you, as soon as you dance with a fellow" (Edna O Brien, The Lonely Girl)

parts.words: "It happens to country like you, as soon as you dance with a fellow" (Edna O Brien, The Lonely Girl)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the missing word is a plural noun for country people, read as 'country ... like you'

explanation.surface: A line of Edna O'Brien dialogue about what happens to country girls when they dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in the quotation; the missing word is a plural noun meaning simple country people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for country bumpkins also means listless sulkers, used by O'Brien of country girls.

clue.text: Maupassant hero in libel (amicably resolved)

indicators.note: the name sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Maupassant character caught up in a defamation case settled out of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'libel (amicably', where the name spans the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Duroy is the scheming title figure of Maupassant's 1885 novel.

clue.text: Ignited by Sillitoe

parts.note: Alan Sillitoe's novel title has something 'on Fire'; ignited stands for 'on fire', so the clue asks what is on fire

explanation.surface: Something set alight by the novelist Alan Sillitoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Sillitoe wrote A Tree on Fire (1967); 'ignited' supplies the 'on fire' part of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing burning in Sillitoe's title is a single woody plant.

clue.text: How Sheila Kaye-Smith would smooth things out, while having a fag?

definitions.text: How Sheila Kaye-Smith would smooth things out, while having a fag?

parts.words: How Sheila Kaye-Smith would smooth things out, while having a fag?
parts.note: a fag is a cigarette, so smoothing out creases while smoking recalls Kaye-Smith's novel title with 'and Smoke'

explanation.surface: A novelist presses her laundry with a cigarette in her mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag is British slang for a cigarette. Sheila Kaye-Smith's novel is Iron and Smoke (1928): to smooth with a flat press while smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing out creases is done with a heated flat tool, the first word of Kaye-Smith's title.

clue.text: Previous English poet

definitions.meaning: Matthew ..., the English poet and diplomat (1664-1721)

explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Prior was an English poet of light verse and epigrams.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means earlier in time and is also the surname of the poet Matthew Prior.

clue.text: Shakespearian knight with connections to former heavyweight

definitions.text: Shakespearian knight with connections to former heavyweight

parts.words: Shakespearian knight with connections to former heavyweight
parts.note: Exton, the knight who kills Richard II, whose first name recalls a famous earlier figure of boxing or letters

explanation.surface: A knight from Shakespeare is linked to a past boxing champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Pierce of Exton murders the king in Richard II.
explanation.definitionFit: Exton is the knight in Richard II who kills the deposed king at Pomfret.

clue.text: You can get evens on a good man being a successful novelist

parts.note: ST stands for saint, a good man
evens is a betting price at even money
taken as written

explanation.surface: A punter is offered even money on a virtuous man becoming a bestselling author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evens' is even-money betting odds, given as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson had great popular success with Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

clue.text: Dramatist comes back during much toasted opening night

indicators.note: the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
the name lies within the words toasted opening

explanation.surface: A playwright returns amid celebrations of his much-praised first night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' points into 'toasted opening', and 'comes back' reads STEDO backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Clifford Odets was the American playwright of Waiting for Lefty and Golden Boy.
